goals: PRIMARY (as posed): estimate nitrate arrival concentrations at drinking-water wells from fertilized-field sources — a lateral source-to-receptor transport goal
FALLBACK (in-scope): quantify vertical nitrate leaching and biogeochemical attenuation (nitrification/denitrification) through the vadose zone beneath representative land-use/soil column types
key_processes: lateral advective-dispersive solute transport from field to well (NOT representable)
N reaction network: nitrification, denitrification, OM respiration/O2 consumption (representable, vertical-only)

model_choice.rationale: The physics is subsurface solute + biogeochemistry, which is a PFLOTRAN reactive-transport question. But the QUESTION'S geometry (field -> well arrival) is lateral, and PFLOTRAN here is 1-D vertical-only with no receptor path, so the model can only address the vertical leaching sub-problem, not the arrival concentration.
model_choice.coupling_note: Even if ELM supplied recharge, there is no ELM->PFLOTRAN SOLUTE coupler, so an ELM-derived fertilizer/N source term cannot drive the chemistry. Inlet N chemistry can only be prescribed.

answerable: vertical nitrate leaching flux and concentration profile vs depth beneath a fertilized column (prescribed inlet chemistry, prescribed/recharge-driven top BC)
relative vadose-zone attenuation (denitrification) between land-use x soil column types
wetting-front / solute travel time to a given depth per soil class

not_answerable.aspect: nitrate ARRIVAL CONCENTRATION at drinking-water wells
not_answerable.why: columns are independent 1-D verticals with no lateral advection, no receptor/well transport path, no capture zone — reactive transport is vertical-only
not_answerable.needs: lateral (2-D/3-D) reactive transport with a well/receptor path

not_answerable.why: no column-to-column exchange and no regional groundwater flow; source and receptor cannot be connected
not_answerable.needs: regional groundwater flow model / lateral routing between columns

not_answerable.aspect: ELM-derived fertilizer/N leaching driving PFLOTRAN chemistry
not_answerable.why: the one-way coupler transfers WATER flux only; no mass/solute hand-off

not_answerable.aspect: validation of nitrate against the external well records
not_answerable.why: no solute observations are wired into the validation path, and the wells are receptors of lateral transport the model cannot produce
not_answerable.needs: solute-observation ingest + lateral transport to a well receptor

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (land use x soil) — applies ONLY to the vertical-leaching fallback goal, NOT to the well-arrival question
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 land-use classes x 3 dominant SSURGO soil classes = 9 column types spans the source-strength and vertical-attenuation axes with one representative column per combination. This is the smallest set that resolves how leaching differs by land use and soil; no replication because the design is diagnostic (relative comparison), and the result cannot answer the actual arrival question regardless of N.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate the fertilized columns on row-crop uplands (dominant land use); oversample poorly-drained fine/high-OM soils where denitrification attenuation is strongest, to bound the vertical-attenuation range. Placement is for CONTRAST, not to connect to any well.
sampling_strategy.replication: none — diagnostic contrast across 9 types; expect solver attrition on extreme soil-contrast columns and report it

sampling_plan.reason: worst-case fast vertical leaching: high N source, low attenuation — bounds maximum deep-transmitted nitrate flux
typical fertilized upland: intermediate vertical travel and attenuation
high N source but strong denitrification — bounds maximum vertical attenuation under fertilization
low source, fast transport — isolates soil effect at reduced N input
background control on strongly attenuating soil

validation_design.comparison: NOT POSSIBLE as co-located — wells are lateral-transport receptors the model cannot produce, and no solute-observation ingest exists in the validation path. At best an ANALOG, qualitative sanity check of simulated vertical leachate magnitude vs shallow-well nitrate, clearly labelled as non-co-located and non-diagnostic
validation_design.metric: qualitative order-of-magnitude only (no defensible bias/RMSE without lateral transport + solute ingest)
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on external well data density; cannot be used as co-located validation regardless

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: prescribed top recharge flux + prescribed inlet N chemistry; CLM-CN / N reaction sandbox (GIRT); native SSURGO soil per column

requires_capabilities.capability: lateral (2-D/3-D) reactive solute transport with well/receptor path
requires_capabilities.why: the question asks for nitrate arrival AT wells from distant fields — inherently lateral
requires_capabilities.blocks: arrival concentration; source-to-receptor linkage — the entire primary question

requires_capabilities.why: no lateral flow between independent 1-D columns
requires_capabilities.blocks: connecting fertilized-field sources to downgradient wells

requires_capabilities.why: existing coupler passes water flux only; no mass hand-off
requires_capabilities.blocks: using an ELM-derived land-surface N leaching source term to drive chemistry

requires_capabilities.capability: solute-observation ingest into the validation path
requires_capabilities.why: well nitrate records cannot currently be confronted with model output
needed to place fertilized-vs-not column types and set source strength
requires_capabilities.blocks: deterministic expansion of the land-use strata

assumptions: Real water table beneath fertilized uplands is within the 50 m PFLOTRAN domain cap; columns deeper than 50 m would pin at the bottom BC and lose depth-to-water meaning.
Inlet N loading must be PRESCRIBED (from agronomic/fertilizer assumptions) since no ELM solute coupler exists; the framework does not derive it.
Elevation relief (160 m) is treated as negligible for forcing; land use, not elevation/climate, is the source-strength driver.
The 9-column ensemble answers only the VERTICAL leaching sub-problem; it does NOT and cannot estimate well arrival concentrations.
open_questions: Given the stack cannot do field-to-well lateral transport, is a reframed VERTICAL question acceptable — e.g. 'how much fertilizer nitrate is transmitted vs denitrified through the vadose zone by land-use/soil type'?
What fertilizer application rate / timing and inlet nitrate concentration should be prescribed at the column top?
Are the external well nitrate records paired with well depths/screens (needed even for an analog comparison)?
Is procuring a lateral groundwater-transport model (e.g. full 3-D PFLOTRAN or a coupled flow model) in scope, since it is required to answer the question as posed?
